reason: C2 is chosen because it proposes a concrete intervention (addition of a small amount of boron), gives a specific mechanism (grain boundary segregation of boron reducing grain boundary energy and enhancing cohesion), makes a quantified prediction (improved toughness and resistance to cracking at high temperatures), and has a clear falsification test (comparing high-temperature toughness of alloys with and without boron addition). While other candidates also propose interventions and mechanisms, C2 stands out for its clarity, specificity, and the direct relevance of its proposed mechanism to the system in question (high-entropy alloys). Additionally, C2's falsification experiment is well-defined, making it a testable hypothesis.
